title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 298 continues the explanation of how the modular group relates to the outer automorphism group of Π_{0,3}, the fundamental group of the projective line minus three points. The previous page set up three things: the action of GP(1,R) = PGL(2,R) on the Poincaré half-plane D, including antiholomorphic maps for negative determinant; the equivalence between a complex elliptic curve E and a pair (V, π), with V a one-dimensional complex vector space and π a lattice; and the canonical orientation of π, meaning a generator η of Λ²_Z π.

This page states the rigidification. A unimodular rigidification of π as a Z-module is the same as a Z-basis (e1, e2) with e1∧e2 = η, that is, an oriented basis. Using e1 to identify V with C (so e1 becomes 1), the rigidified curve becomes a single number τ = e2 in C. Two conditions follow:
- (1, τ) spans a discrete rank-2 subgroup exactly when τ is not real (Im τ ≠ 0).
- The basis (1, τ) is positively oriented exactly when Im τ > 0, so τ lies in D.

The set of isomorphism classes of rigidified elliptic curves is therefore identified with D. Changing the basis by a matrix (a b; c d) acts by the Möbius map τ ↦ (aτ+b)/(cτ+d), which is the natural action of SL(2,Z) on D. It factors through SL(2,Z)' = SL(2,Z)/{±1}, identified with GP(1,Z)^+ = PSL(2,Z).

The page then says this group acts properly on D with exactly two critical (elliptic) orbits. The next page completes this: the orbits are those of i (lattice Z[i], stabilizer of order 2) and of j = e^{2πi/3} (lattice Z[j], order 3). The quotient D/PSL(2,Z) is then identified with the projective line minus one point, normalized so the order-3 orbit goes to ∞, the order-2 orbit to 1 and the cusp to 0. This gives an isomorphism between the orbifold fundamental group of D modulo the group and the fundamental group of Y with that ramification data.

Purpose: to make the dictionary between Out(Π_{0,3}) ≅ GL(2,Z)/±1 and the modular group / moduli of elliptic curves explicit, as background for the 'équation des lacets' and the Teichmüller tower in genus 0 and 1. This is classical material: the upper half-plane as the Teichmüller space of genus 1 and the j-line as the moduli orbifold.
errors: SL(2,Z) itself does not act faithfully on D, since -1 acts trivially. The correct statement is SL(2,Z)/{±1} ≅ GP(1,Z)^+. The prime in Grothendieck's notation SL(2,Z)' (meaning modulo ±1) handles this, but the machine transcription drops the prime.
Minor: the note '(comme base de V sur C)' should presumably read 'sur R'. A Z-basis of the lattice is an R-basis of V; as a C-space V is one-dimensional. The reading is uncertain.

ideas.what: Elliptic curves with an oriented basis of H_1 (unimodular rigidification) are parametrized by τ in the upper half-plane.
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller space of genus 1 = upper half-plane; framed elliptic curves
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (discussion of the modular tower); not explicitly written there

ideas.what: PSL(2,Z) acts by Möbius transformations with two elliptic orbits (i, of order 2, and ρ, of order 3); the quotient is the j-line, with the cusp as the remaining point.
ideas.modern_name: Modular orbifold M_{1,1}; j-invariant; PSL(2,Z) ≅ C2 * C3

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine textbook recapitulation of the modular action on the upper half-plane, written as preparation for explicit computations with Out(Π_{0,3}). Nothing on the page is new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: 'élément e2=τ de 𝔼[?]' should read 'de ℂ'.
'on trouve SL(2,Z) ≃ GP(1,Z)^+' should read 'Sl(2,Z)' ≃ GP(1,Z)^+', with a prime marking the quotient by ±1.
'sur {+l'une+} [-les-] classes[?] d'isomorphie' likely reads 'sur l'ensemble des classes d'isomorphie de courbes ell. rigidifiées, identifié à D'.
Insertion '(comme base de V sur C)' may be '... sur R' (uncertain).
The first line is a continuation of 'Le choix d'une rigidification' from the previous page: 'de forme unimodulaire de π' (lower-case π, the lattice).
